questions.q: 'He worked day and night so that he ___ support his family.' may/might?
questions.a: 'might' — past main clause drags the purpose modal back. A wrong answer 'may' ignores the zone-harmony.

questions.q: 'I will phone you as soon as I ___ (reach) home.'
questions.a: 'reach' — future time-clauses use present form; 'will reach' is banned after 'as soon as'. The Hindi-transfer error.

questions.q: 'She said that she ___ come the next day.' will/would?
questions.a: 'would' — past reporting zone shifts will→would. A wrong answer 'will' keeps the speaker's modal instead of the reporter's.

questions.q: Purpose clauses take may/might, not will/______ confusions.

Fill in the blank: In complex ______ the subordinate tense must harmonize with the main: past main → past-family subordinates ('He worked hard so that he might pass'); present/future main → free subordinates.
Fill in the blank: The ______-clause rule: 'He studies so that he may pass' (present main) vs 'He studied so that he might pass' (past main) — may→might follows the zone.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student applies tense harmony across object, purpose, result, and time clauses — including might-for-past-purpose and the truth-exemption.
